description: Render JSX, HTML, or a node tree to PNG/JPEG/WebP/SVG and animations. Rust core with JS, WASM, and native bindings.
rules: Prefer `render(node, options)` from `takumi-js`, or `new ImageResponse(node, options)` from `takumi-js/response` in a route handler. Both reuse one renderer across calls, so a module-level `Renderer` singleton is unnecessary.

Import from `takumi-js`, not `@takumi-rs/core` or `@takumi-rs/wasm`. It picks the native addon on Node.js and Bun and WebAssembly on edge runtimes and loads it itself, so leave out `initSync`, `?module` imports, and reading a `.wasm` file.
`ImageResponse` streams its body, so a `try`/`catch` around `new ImageResponse(...)` never sees a render error. Await `response.ready` and return a fallback when it rejects.

Takumi never reads system fonts. Its one built-in font is Geist, Latin only, weights 300 to 800. Pass every other font per call through `fonts`, and load Google Fonts with `googleFonts` from `takumi-js/helpers`, which fetches only the subsets the text needs.

A `fonts` entry is a URL string, raw bytes, or `{ name, data, weight, style, generic, unicodeRange }`, where `data` is bytes or a function returning them. Leave `weight` out for a variable font, which then serves its whole `wght` axis. Register it once, not once per weight.
Pass images through `images: [{ src: "logo", data }]` and use the key as `src` or in `url()`. Remote URLs are fetched for you. Do not inline them as base64 data URLs.
Pass CSS, including compiled Tailwind, through `css`. `stylesheets` is deprecated.
The root element does not fill the canvas on its own. Set `width: 100%` and `height: 100%` on it.
The `tw` prop is a built-in Tailwind subset with no Preflight, so elements keep their UA margins.

Takumi is not Satori. A `<div>` is `display: block` as in a browser, and block, inline, float, flex, grid, and table layout all work. `<style>` rules, `var()`, `oklch()`, `color-mix()`, gradients, `mask`, `clip-path`, `filter`, variable fonts, and inline `<svg>` work too, so do not work around them.
In Rust, import from `takumi::prelude` and build options with `RenderOptions::builder()`. Fonts live in a `Fonts` context, not a global one.
Code samples carry Fumadocs annotations such as `// [!code --]` and `// [!code highlight]`. Never copy them into generated code, and treat `[!code --]` lines as the removed API.
